text: When designing REST APIs, following best practices is essential for creating reliable and easy-to-use services. First, choose clear and meaningful endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened; for example, use 200 for success, 404 for a missing resource, and 500 for server errors. Third, provide complete documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and possible responses. Finally, use versioning, such as /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. These simple habits make your API easier to maintain and help developers integrate with it successfully.
